doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Closing: still working at 83, moving to Las Vegas
summary: Levy says he cannot retire, has moved to Las Vegas near Joe and Nancy, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well, this has been a fascinating discussion. We’ve been talking with John Levy, who has seen the music business from a lot of different angles here, and it’s really been great talking to you.
Well it’s been a pleasure, truly, it’s really been a pleasure, Monk, to really sit and talk about it. I just wish I could have prepared a little better.
Well, you had some great thoughts.

Yeah, a little preparation, but you called me kind of sudden and I said — oh, what are we going to talk about? I’ve got to get all my facts together here. Because this year I’m 83 years old, so, you know you don’t remember things so well, you know.

It kind of catches up with you, and people say to me, “why are you still doing this — why don’t you retire?” I say, “retire to what? What am I going to retire to? This is the greatest life in the world.”
Yeah, you tell them, you see this, you know where I was when I did this video? So don’t tell me about working too hard.

That’s right. That’s absolutely right. So I really you know, enjoy it. I enjoy the business and I enjoy the music part of it. And I wouldn’t know what to do with myself to retire. I recently moved to Las Vegas and everybody says “why did you go to Las Vegas” you know. I say, “well, for several reasons,” I say, “one of them was taxes, the other one was earthquakes,” and so—
And you can play golf with Joe.

Yeah. I can play golf with Joe. I’m close to Joe and now Nancy bought a condominium there, so I says so I’ve got my clients right there with me. You know we all enjoy the Las Vegas weather and just taking it easy. You know we’re at that stage where we sort of coast on it a little bit, and we’re not out there fighting it every day. So it’s enjoyable. I enjoy it very much. And it’s been a pleasure doing this. And I make a point — I’m coming next time. I want to come to your school next time.
All right. Great. We’ll see you at Hamilton College. And as part of our Jazz Archive, it’s been a real pleasure to talk to John Levy today. Thank you very much.
